definition.description: On an inspected, dry, stable uphill lane with a declared gentle-to-moderate grade, perform a short sequence of alternating forward bounds. Each contact projects the body uphill with controlled foot placement, hip extension, trunk organisation, and a planned walk-down recovery. This excludes uphill sprinting, jogging, straight-leg bounds, bilateral hops, downhill bounds, weighted bounds, or an unspecified steep grade.

environment.surface: inspected dry stable uphill lane with no holes, loose material, cross-slope, traffic, or unsafe weather; flat controlled start and finish areas
environment.space: one athlete at a time in the uphill lane; a separated walk-down recovery route with no cross traffic
inspection: inspect grade, surface, traction, weather, visibility, lane, finish, and walk-down route
mark start and finish; declare grade, contact count or duration, and walk-down recovery
remove bystanders and prevent downhill jogging through the active lane
confirm footwear, communication, stop signal, and current running/bounding exposure
environment.changeRule: Changing grade, surface, traction, direction, contact sequence, distance, duration, pace, load, recovery route, or purpose requires revalidation.

selectionPrerequisites: controlled level alternating bounds and pain-free tolerance of current hill-running and ankle/calf/tibial loading
safe inspected lane, grade, finish, and walk-down route
current lower-limb, tendon, impact, and session-fatigue budgets fit
understands the bound pattern, route, stop signal, and full recovery rule
excludeOrEscalate: symptom, restriction, unsafe grade, traction, weather, visibility, surface, footwear, lane, finish, recovery route, or communication conflict
pain, giving way, dizziness, neurologic, circulation, breathing, chest, balance, or communication concern
notEstablishedByEvidence: universal grade, contact count, duration, recovery, impact reduction, readiness threshold, output, or clinical clearance

provenance.identityAuthority: Source 995 plus alternating-bounds-v1 evidence packet. Uphill Bound is a candidate incline delivery of alternating bounds; grade-specific identity, media, and all approvals remain subject to qualified human review.

anatomy.laterality: alternating left-right unilateral contacts with bilateral trunk and arm organisation
anatomy.claimsBoundary: Task mechanics and likely loading sites only; no diagnosis, treatment, injury-prevention, isolated activation, or guaranteed performance claim.

athleteSupport.whyItMatters: Candidate incline alternating-bound exposure when the exact grade, surface, contact pattern, recovery route, and session budgets fit.
athleteSupport.primaryCue: Push the hill away, keep contacts under you, and stop before the bounds become slow running.
secondaryCues: use the declared lane and walk down to recover
stay tall through the trunk rather than folding into the hill
keep the alternating rhythm and controlled foot placement
do not treat a steeper hill as an automatic progression
expectedSensations: brief propulsive hip, calf, thigh, trunk, and foot effort
short high-intent alternating contacts with full recovery
unexpectedSensations: foot, ankle, calf, tibial, knee, hip, back, or shoulder pain
slipping, giving way, dizziness, unsafe traffic, or a pattern that turns into slow running
selfChecks: lane, grade, finish, and walk-down route are clear
each contact remains alternating and underneath the body

observationChecklist: exact short uphill alternating-bound identity, not sprinting, jogging, straight-leg bounds, bilateral hops, downhill, or weighted work
grade, surface, traction, weather, lane, finish, walk-down route, footwear, and spacing
alternating rhythm, foot strike, hip extension, posture, projection, symptoms, and first quality loss

faultCorrections.slow_running_stride_or_lost_bound_patter: reduce contacts, grade, or intensity; restore short alternating bounds and full recovery; stop if the pattern does not return
faultCorrections.excessive_forward_fold_or_overstride: reduce grade or distance, restore tall trunk and contact under the body, or stop
faultCorrections.slip_or_unsafe_walk_down: stop and correct the lane, traction, or recovery route; do not count or continue unsafe attempts

doNotUseWhen: uphill sprinting, jogging, straight-leg bounds, bilateral hops, downhill bounds, weighted bounds, or a steep grade is intended
the hill, weather, traction, lane, finish, or recovery route is unsafe
the exact task conflicts with symptoms, restrictions, or current lower-limb/tendon/impact fatigue budget

supportOperations.supportEscalation: Stop unresolved grade, surface, weather, logistics, identity, symptom, or quality concerns and follow facility escalation policy.
supportOperations.changeImpactPolicy: Any change to grade, surface, contacts, distance, duration, recovery, dose, or substitution reruns selection, logistics, duration, fatigue, substitutions, and validation.

snapshot.description: The athlete bounds uphill for a short distance with powerful hip extension, tall posture, and full recovery between reps.

programmingProfile.stimulusDose: short high-intent alternating uphill bounds with walk-down recovery

deliveryProfiles.purpose: Candidate short-duration incline alternating-bound work when the exact lane, grade, pattern, recovery route, and lower-limb exposure budget fit.

dosage.countRule: count only alternating bounds on the declared uphill lane that retain controlled posture, contact pattern, projection, finish, and walk-down recovery

deliveryProfiles.qualityGate: Every counted attempt retains the declared grade and safe lane, alternating bound pattern, controlled foot placement and trunk position, safe finish/walk-down route, and no stop event.
stopRules: stop on pain, giving way, slipping, unsafe surface/weather/lane/finish/recovery route, dizziness, loss of balance, or participant request
stop when the alternating bound pattern, cadence, posture, contact control, or projection cannot be restored
stop when the drill becomes slow running or fatigue conditioning rather than short high-quality bounds
deliveryProfiles.coachInstructions: Inspect and declare grade, surface, traction, weather, lane, start, finish, contacts/duration, route, and rest; observe from side and rear when safe; stop at first unrecoverable quality or safety loss.
deliveryProfiles.athleteInstructions: Use the declared uphill lane, bound with alternating contacts, push the hill away while staying tall, finish under control, and walk down on the assigned route before the next attempt.
deliveryProfiles.expectedAdaptation: Candidate task-specific incline alternating-bound exposure only; no universal power, speed, running, or injury outcome is guaranteed.

doseScaling.reduce: fewer contacts, gentler grade, shorter lane, lower intent, longer rest, or another reviewed task after revalidation
doseScaling.doNotAutoProgress: Do not increase grade, distance, duration, speed, load, downhill return, straight-leg strategy, or turn this into hill sprinting without revalidation.

supportPrompts.athlete: Push the hill away, alternate cleanly, walk down to recover.
supportPrompts.coach: Confirm grade, surface, and bound identity before counting an attempt.
